notes.title: Chapter 2: LAST SEQUENCE BEING PROGRAMMED!
notes.notes:
Hey everyone,

Since graduating uni, I’ve been working hard on Chapter 2 of The Designer’s Curse, and it’s shaping up really well! I’m genuinely proud of the atmosphere, the gameplay, and how everything is coming together. I even used the game as my final research project at uni, writing a lot of the music for it. Plus, my dad and I did some voice acting, which was a lot of fun!

So yeah… things are looking SUPER CLOSE now! Can you believe it?!

Also, I know I promised some of you free keys for Chapter 2, but… it’s been a while, and I totally forgot who I offered them to LOL. If I promised you one, just message me with proof when the game releases, and I’ll make sure you get a Steam key!

Thanks for sticking with me (5 years, I know... LOL). You guys are the best. Trailer coming soon, followed by THE ACTUAL GAME!!

notes.title: Chapter 2 won't be released for a while.
notes.notes:
Hi guys,

Thank you so much for the always appreciated support. Unfortunately, school and work have been prioritised over game development, so I highly doubt that I will be able to release chapter 2 this year. I know this will come as a disappointment, but please know that this comes from me wanting to release a game that is genuinely fun and enjoyable. It will be a paid game and I want it to be worth it. 

When are we talking? not sure. I can't see it releasing later than summer 2022, but I aim to get it out around springtime 2022. 

Why does this expected time of release keep changing? As a game developer, I am optimistic about my performance. But unfortunately, I have underestimated the amount of time needed to work on my school work. 

Also, any messages of encouragement are and will always be appreciated. And thanks so much for supporting me!

This WILL happen!

Christian.

notes.title: About the physics. Maybe multiplayer in the future?
notes.notes:
Hey guys,

Just to keep you updated, in lockdown I've had lots of time to work on the game and it's been going well. I wanted you all to know that by popular demand I've redone the whole door system. Just to clarify, these updates will only be in the second chapter and I don't think there will be a chance that I will revamp the first chapter.

So, what did I fix? well, before, opening doors from the pull side was easy. However, the push side was a pain. You'd have to get the right angle, and look in a certain place, or walk at the same time, and it was so annoying. I've written an algorithm that works much better, still, click and drag, but the directional stuff works way better. It will the same for doors, chests, and wardrobes (You know, how you previously couldn't open a chest when crouching, that sort of stuff).

I'm researching into how difficult multiplayer could be. like I non-canon mini-game to have fun with friends where one of them is a monster. Just a little fun I could possibly put in, as people love that kind of thing. Don't get your hopes up though, it's just an idea and I have no clue what I'm doing when it comes to that.

Thanks for all the support

notes.title: Chapter 2 more updates and details
notes.notes:
Hi all,
So, good news. I have a new laptop which allows me to work on the game away from home (as I spend a lot of time at school). I continued the project last week after a long break and it's safe to say it's going well. Here are some features you can hope for in chapter 2-
-	Less frustrating moments where not being caught does not become a task which slowly begins to be more frustrating than scary
-	More creative puzzles that don't just revolve around getting a key or code.
-	Exciting story that leaves you wanting to know more.
-	It could be said that the game play would be more fun, and some levels with an element of pure puzzle rather than constant fear.
-	About 2 hours gameplay, for either 99 cents or $1.99.
-	You can’t lean through walls (Sorry)       
Release month approximate – July-September 2020.
Thanks for your patience.

notes.title: When is chapter 2 coming?
notes.notes:
Hey everyone,

Things for chapter 2 are quite difficult, I have lots of schoolwork now that I’ve got A levels so it's pretty hard to tackle. I'm a one person team and that’s slowly catching up to me. I don't think It will be available until late spring next year, however- this is purely for the sake of me being able to make it as good as it can be. 

Though the publicity of the game has not gone as I expected, being that not many big gaming youtubers check steam anymore and mainly rely on itchio for horror games, which is a problem because itch.io refuses to put my game on any listings at all. It’s a little bit disheartening to see so much work literally be ignored by their website, but I thank steam’s algorithm for being so kind and putting my game up on the top of listings.

Not to worry, I’m getting it sorted. Chapter 2 is in the works. It’s just taking a while.

notes.title: Chapter 2 Updates + amazing workshop guide!
notes.notes:
Hey guys,

Thanks so much for the amazing support on this project. It means the world to me that people are even playing it, and the criticisms I’m receiving are so helpful and will genuinely help me to make the next chapter as awesome as I can.

Speaking of which, I’m starting the design’s now for chapter 2. I’m going to sell the new chapters for about 99p for about 2-3 hours gameplay per chapter (not just finding keys and flipping levers this time, I really want some interesting mechanics and puzzles) :)

Of course this takes a while, and I’m a child that still goes to school and had a life and can’t spend all day coding games other wise he’ll put on a few pounds. So obviously it will take a bit of time! I’m aiming for February next year or sooner (hopefully).

An amazing community guide has been created by “Maowcraft”. It’s thoroughly detailed and awesome and you can check it out here- 
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1825599983

(Although there’s one incorrect fact mentioning that “Albert” is the “master” when in fact Albert is someone completely different. I’m sure theorists can work that out 😉)
